messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Iterations start fast but become very slow
parts:
Hi Marcelo,

Without the data + program, I can only give generic advice:
- simulate data from the model and make sure that fits
- start with a smaller data set
- do posterior predictive checks once you have it fit on simulated data
- make sure the gradients are well behaved for a few of the starting points
- standardize your parameters
- wait longer


Daniel

Hi, I have a problem running Stan. Iterations begin well: 0%, 10%, 20%, ... but by 30% it starts to take a long time! Very much! More and more the delay increases. Does anyone know what I could check in my code?

Thank you.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Iterations start fast but become very slow
parts:
If you have the default 50% warmup, what you're probably seeing
is that as Stan adapts the mass matrix (essentially scale of each
parameter), it is having to take a very small step size and the
number of steps go up. This is usually because there's some
parameter bumping up against a boundary (which forces it to try to
run off to positive or negative infinity on the unconstrained scale
where Stan samples), or because there's very high curvature in some
regions of the posterior.

- Bob
